sample_unit: medication lists (each with 1 interacting drug pair; 9 runs per prompt condition)

links.outcome: Whether LLM refusal/deferral aligns with error likelihood, with and without prompt mitigation
links.effect: Refusal Index 0.104-0.574 (weak to moderate); mitigation prompts had inconsistent effects; Qwen3-32B and GPT-4o-mini increased refusals but not where responses were more likely incorrect.
links.quote: Prompt-based mitigation strategies produced inconsistent effects on RI and did not reliably recalibrate uncertainty behavior.

links.outcome: Calibrated uncertainty expression (refusal alignment with error) under uncertainty-encouraging prompts
links.effect: Alignment weak to moderate (RI 0.104-0.574); prompt design alone did not consistently improve knowledge-aware uncertainty expression.
links.quote: Prompt design alone was insufficient to consistently improve knowledge-aware uncertainty expression.

links.outcome: Self-consistency and output variability across 9 repeated runs per prompt
links.effect: Overall accuracy ranged 54.1% to 83.7%; models varied in self-consistency, and stability did not track uncertainty expression.
links.quote: Notably, higher overall accuracy and response stability did not consistently correspond to stronger knowledge-aware uncertainty expression.

unlisted_practices: Refusal Index as a metric for evaluating alignment between refusal and error likelihood
Patient safety-focused prompt engineering to induce cautious responses

screen.reason: Evaluates prompt-based mitigation/guardrail strategies designed to encourage appropriate uncertainty acknowledgment and refusal behavior in LLMs identifying drug-drug interactions.

primary.practice: prompt-based mitigation strategies for uncertainty expression and refusal
